transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’ve ruined everything in my life and I don’t deserve to be doing art or working with anyone anymore. I've let everyone down so badly, and I just feel like I should stay out of everyone's way.
Have you felt this deep sense of hopelessness and low mood for most of the past two years, or is this a distinct period that started more recently?

It’s been going on for almost two years now, settling in about midway through the first year after my divorce. This crushing sadness has been there for the vast majority of that time, with only really brief, blurry moments where I didn't feel completely weighed down by it.
During these past two years, have there been any periods lasting longer than two months where your mood improved significantly or you felt like your usual self?

No, I haven't had any long breaks like that at all. Last summer there were maybe a few weeks where the heavy sadness lifted a little bit, but even then I didn't feel like my normal self. It's just been this constant, heavy weight for almost the whole time.
Have you experienced other symptoms during this time, such as changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, or feeling constantly tired and low on energy?

Yes, my appetite is all over the place—I barely eat and have lost a lot of weight, though sometimes I'll suddenly binge late at night. Sleep is awful too; I lie awake for hours with my mind spinning and then wake up at 4 AM with a jolt of dread. I feel completely drained all the time, like my body is made of sandbags and even showering wipes me out.
Have these feelings of worthlessness and the physical exhaustion been so severe that you have had thoughts of ending your life or felt that life is no longer worth living?

Yes, quite often, especially on the really dark nights when I think it would just be better for everyone if I didn't wake up. I've even found myself Googling painless ways to die and imagining how I'd do it. But I always get scared and close the laptop before actually making any kind of plan.

During these past two years, have there been times when your mood and energy were so severely low that you were unable to function at all, perhaps even losing touch with reality or needing hospitalization?

Yes, there were times when the crushing sadness and complete lack of energy happened right alongside hearing that harsh voice and feeling convinced I was being blacklisted. It made functioning impossible—I ended up quitting my freelance work, falling behind on rent, and completely withdrawing from everyone. I've never been hospitalized, but during those times I felt entirely shut down and disconnected from reality.
When you heard that voice and felt convinced you were being blacklisted, did those experiences occur only during your most severe episodes of depression, or did they happen at other times as well?

They actually happened even when I wasn't feeling deeply depressed. Last summer, there was a period of a few weeks where my mood lifted and I didn't feel particularly sad or numb, but I still heard that harsh voice at night and felt completely convinced people were sharing warnings about me.

During those weeks when your mood felt better, were you also experiencing other symptoms like disorganized thinking, a lack of motivation to do things, or a significant decrease in your ability to express emotions?

No, during those weeks my motivation actually improved a bit and my thoughts didn't feel particularly jumbled or hard to express. But even though the heavy sadness had lifted, I was still hearing that harsh voice at night and remained absolutely convinced that people were secretly blacklisting me.

During the periods when your mood felt better and you were not depressed, did you experience any other unusual symptoms, such as seeing things that weren't there, feeling like people were monitoring you, or believing you had special powers or significance?

I never felt like I had any special powers, but I definitely felt like people were monitoring and blacklisting me online. Even when my mood was a bit better, that harsh voice at night was still there telling me I was a fraud. It was just those same things persisting, even without the deep sadness.

During those weeks when your mood felt better, did you experience any periods of disorganized speech, a lack of emotional expression, or a significant decline in your ability to take care of your daily responsibilities?

During those weeks last summer, my mood was definitely a bit better, but I still had the voice and that paranoia. As for having disorganized speech, a lack of emotional expression, or trouble with daily responsibilities, I'm not really sure or don't remember if I struggled with those during that specific brief period.

Looking back at those weeks last summer when your mood felt better, do you recall if the voice and the belief that you were being blacklisted occurred every single day, or were they present only occasionally?

They were happening pretty much every day, not just occasionally. Even though the heavy sadness had lifted for a bit, I still heard that harsh voice every night and the constant feeling that I was being blacklisted didn't stop at all. It was really unsettling because those things just wouldn't leave me alone.
Did these daily experiences of hearing the voice and feeling blacklisted persist for at least two weeks while you were not experiencing any significant mood symptoms?

Yes, they definitely lasted for at least two weeks. During that period last summer, my mood had lifted and I didn't feel especially sad or numb, but I was still hearing that harsh voice every night and remained convinced that people were sharing warnings about me online.

During that two-week period when you were not depressed but still heard the voice and felt blacklisted, did you also experience a significant loss of interest in almost all activities, or did you feel capable of enjoying things and engaging with your life?

During that time last summer, I actually felt a bit more capable of doing things and didn't have that same heavy loss of interest. I didn't feel as sad, numb, or weighed down as I usually do. But even though I felt more able to engage, I was still hearing that harsh voice and felt completely convinced I was being blacklisted.

During that two-week period when you were not depressed, did you experience any other symptoms like a lack of emotional expression, disorganized thinking, or a total withdrawal from social interaction?

No, I don't recall having disorganized thinking, flat emotions, or totally withdrawing from people during those specific weeks, as my mood felt a bit lighter then. But I was definitely still hearing that harsh voice at night and felt completely convinced that people were blacklisting me.

Aside from the voices and the belief about being blacklisted, did you experience any persistent lack of motivation, difficulty speaking, or a sense that your emotions were 'flat' or 'blunted' for a longer period of time, such as over several months?

Yes, for well over a year, I've had a severe lack of motivation and a heavy, flat, "gray" emotional state where I just lie on the couch and ignore invites because nothing seems worth the effort. I've also struggled a lot with speaking, because it takes forever for the thoughts in my head to turn into words, which causes really long pauses when I try to talk to my friends.
